messages:
Owen Park: Hey team, first-day device arrived (ThinkPad T14s). During OOB it's asking to enroll with our Linux fleet agent but the installer errors with 'TPM2 not detected' and the LUKS setup failed midway. Now the machine boots to a busybox shell. Anyone run into this on company ThinkPads?
Rina Shah (IT): welcome! serial? sometimes vendor firmware ships with BitLocker/LUKS remnants or a firmware lock. serial and screenshot of the busybox error would help.
Owen Park: serial X1T14S-9Z88. Busybox prompt shows: "/bin/sh: can't access '/lib/systemd/systemd'" and a small note: "cryptsetup: unexpected token in header".
mdm-bot: Device X1T14S9Z88: provisioning failed during linux-auto-enroll. Agent installer v1.4.2 returned exit code 42. TPM inventory shows missing in MDM record.
Rina Shah (IT): hmm. couple of quick checks: 1) does the firmware show TPM enabled in BIOS/UEFI? 2) is Secure Boot on? we require TPM and secureboot for LUKS escrowing to KMS.
Owen Park: I can get to UEFI but it's asking for supervisor password (vendor set one). I don't have that.
it-ops-bot: Note: vendor-supplied firmware passwords must be cleared by Hardware Ops. Please open ticket: "UEFI supervisor PW clear for <serial>". We can expedite for on-boarding.
Owen Park: opened IT-2329: "UEFI supervisor PW clear for X1T14S-9Z88".
Rina Shah (IT): good. while hardware ops handles that I'll explain the usual flow: once TPM is enabled and attested, MDM pushes the fleet agent which runs: sudo ./fleet-install.sh --enroll https://fleet.redwood-internal/enroll && sudo cryptsetup luksFormat /dev/nvme0n1p3 --type luks2. If the header is corrupt we re-create and restore keys from our key escrow if present.
secure-boot-bot: Device X1T14S9Z88: Secure Boot disabled (UEFI reports). LUKS header mismatch detected. Recovery key not found in escrow (pre-enroll failure).
Rina Shah (IT): since recovery key wasn't escrowed (enroll failed), we have two options: 1) Hardware team clears supervisor PW so you can enable TPM+SecureBoot and re-run enroll (preferred, may be fastest). 2) If you prefer not to wait, we can image a replacement drive and pre-seed the key and image. Which would you prefer?
Owen Park: prefer to avoid losing data (I had a couple local notes), but it's a fresh laptop so not much on it. Happy to image a replacement drive if that's faster. How long for hardware ops?
Kai Morgan: hardware ops here. if you want a clean image we can stage a pre-provisioned NVMe and swap via mail express same-day if you're in the city. Clearing supervisor PW is ~90 minutes remote with vendor tools but needs physical presence from me to open the chassis (firmware password removal procedure). I can do either today.
Owen Park: express swap sounds fine if faster. I can drop the old drive in a return envelope.
Kai Morgan: cool. I'll start prepping the pre-provisioned drive (enterprise image with fleet agent and LUKS header already escrowed). ETA 3 hours.
Rina Shah (IT): once you boot the pre-provisioned image you'll see the join flow. If anything asks for a key you can check the escrow via: curl -s https://kms.redwood-internal/keys/X1T14S9Z88 | jq .luks_key_id (requires VPN).
Owen Park: thanks. curious: why would the TPM not be detected? vendor defect?
Rina Shah (IT): usually either TPM disabled in UEFI, firmware bug, or vendor had a custom provisioning that interferes. We log it and follow up with vendor. We'll also add a step to the vendor checklist to verify TPM presence before shipping.
mdm-bot: IT-2329 updated: hardware ops initiated pre-provisioned drive replacement. Pre-provisioning job id: pp-4932.
Owen Park: awesome, thanks everyone. I'll wait for Kai's note and then try the pre-provisioned drive. Appreciate the quick responses :raised_hands:
Kai Morgan: shipping label and instructions sent via IT-2329. Ping if you want pickup instead of dropoff.
Rina Shah (IT): and once you're up, ping me and I'll approve temporary sudo for 48h to install your dev container stuff. Welcome aboard!
Owen Park: will do, excited to get started :rocket:
